Will County Circuit Court

Are you facing a legal issue in Will County and wondering where to go for a fair resolution? The Will County Circuit Court is your answer. As one of the busiest courts in Illinois, it serves as the forum for resolving various civil and criminal cases. In this article, we will provide a comprehensive guide to the Will County Circuit Court.

What is the Will County Circuit Court?

The Will County Circuit Court is a court of general jurisdiction in the Twelfth Judicial Circuit of Illinois. It is located in the Will County Courthouse in Joliet and presided over by 16 Circuit Judges elected by the citizens of Will County. The Court is divided into several divisions, including the Civil Division, Criminal Division, Family Division, and Probate Division.

What Types of Cases are Handled by the Will County Circuit Court?

The Will County Circuit Court handles various types of civil and criminal cases, including:

Civil Cases

The Civil Division of the Court handles civil cases, including:

  • Personal injury claims
  • Contract disputes
  • Property damage claims
  • Landlord-tenant disputes
  • Small claims cases

Criminal Cases

The Criminal Division of the Court handles criminal cases, including:

  • Felony cases
  • Misdemeanor cases
  • Traffic cases
  • Juvenile delinquency cases

Family Cases

The Family Division of the Court handles family law cases, including:

  • Divorce cases
  • Child custody cases
  • Child support cases
  • Adoption cases
  • Paternity cases

Probate Cases

The Probate Division of the Court handles probate cases, including:

  • Estate administration
  • Guardianship cases
  • Mental health cases

How to File a Case in the Will County Circuit Court?

To file a case in the Will County Circuit Court, you need to follow these steps:

  1. Determine which division of the Court your case falls under.
  2. Obtain the necessary forms from the Court's website or the Clerk's office.
  3. Fill out the forms accurately and completely.
  4. Pay the filing fee.
  5. File the forms with the Clerk's office.
  6. Serve the other party with the necessary documents.

What are the Court's Rules and Procedures?

The Will County Circuit Court has various rules and procedures that must be followed to ensure a fair and efficient resolution of cases. Some of the rules and procedures include:

  • Rules of Civil Procedure
  • Rules of Criminal Procedure
  • Rules of Evidence
  • Local Court Rules

How to Find a Will County Circuit Court Case?

To find a Will County Circuit Court case, you can use the Court's online case search tool, which allows you to search for cases by name, case number, or date filed. You can also visit the Clerk's office to obtain copies of court records.

What are the Court's Hours of Operation?

The Will County Circuit Court is open from Monday to Friday, from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, excluding holidays.
